title: Symmetric mass generation of interacting chiral fermions on a one-dimensional lattice without fermion doubling
authors: V. A. Zakharov, Atsushi Ueda, Frank Verstraete, C. W. J. Beenakker
abstract: Symmetric mass generation is the interaction-induced opening of a fermion gap without spontaneous symmetry breaking. The anomaly-free 3-4-5-0 model of Wang and Wen provides a minimal one-dimensional setting for this phenomenon, but a direct lattice realization faces two obstacles: fermion doubling for local chiral discretizations and perturbative irrelevance of the six-fermion gapping interaction. We address both obstacles. First, we formulate the model on a strictly one-dimensional tangent-fermion lattice, where a nonlocal hopping produces a single chiral branch without a mirror partner while retaining an efficient tensor-network representation. Second, we add a Hubbard-type density-density interaction (Luttinger parameter $K$) that reduces the scaling dimension of the 3-4-5-0 interaction from $5$ to $5K$, making it relevant for $K<2/5$. Density-matrix renormalization group calculations show the opening of an excitation gap in this regime without the appearance of a degenerate ground state, the hallmark of symmetric mass generation.
summary: The paper tackles the challenge of achieving symmetric mass generation for chiral fermions on a lattice by modifying the standard model. It introduces a Hubbard interaction term that renders the gapping mechanism perturbatively relevant. Through theoretical analysis and DMRG simulations, the authors confirm that this setup successfully opens an excitation gap without breaking any underlying symmetries.
main_problem: The research addresses how symmetric mass generation (SMG)—opening a fermion gap without spontaneous symmetry breaking—can be achieved in a minimal 1D lattice model.
main_result: By combining a modified chiral fermionic model with a Hubbard-type interaction, the authors demonstrate that SMG occurs when the effective Luttinger parameter $K$ is sufficiently small ($K < 2/5$).
method: The analysis combines bosonization techniques to analyze low-energy continuum limits and Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) calculations for numerical verification.
model_or_system: The system involves interacting chiral fermions described by the anomaly-free 3–4–5–0 model on a tangent-fermion lattice. The Hamiltonian is modified by adding a Hubbard-type density-density interaction to make the gapping term relevant.
key_observables: Opening of an excitation gap ($\Delta$) while maintaining a non-degenerate ground state, and the smoothing of power-law singularities in the momentum occupation factor $n_\alpha(k)$.
important_parameters: The Luttinger parameter $K$, which must satisfy $K < 2/5$ for the interaction to become relevant.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that tuning the Hubbard interaction can make the gapping perturbation visible at accessible system sizes, and it utilizes tangent fermions to avoid fermion doubling issues.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the chiral fermion dispersion relation, compare gap opening signatures (SMG vs. SSB), and show DMRG results demonstrating the smoothing of Luttinger-liquid singularities in the gapped regime.
paper_structure: The paper first reformulates the model to address lattice artifacts (doubling) and interaction irrelevance; it then uses bosonization to analyze scaling dimensions, showing how the Hubbard term renormalizes the coupling; finally, DMRG calculations confirm the gap opening signature characteristic of SMG.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete theoretical realization of interacting topological phases in 1D systems, using techniques (bosonization, DMRG) highly relevant to strongly correlated electron physics and quantum impurity models.

FIG. 2. Comparison of the expected dependence on the sys- tem size L of the excitation energy ∆(energy of an excited state relative to the ground state). Panel I shows the finite- size gap ∆∝1/L in a system that is gapless in the thermo- dynamic limit (a flat line when ∆× L is plotted versus L). Panels II and III compare a gapped system with (II) or with- out (III) the appearance of a degenerate ground state. In case II, the symmetry is broken when E1 merges with the ground state, leaving a gap to the next level E2. Case III represents symmetric mass generation (SMG).

FIG. 3. DMRG results for the energies of the two lowest excited states E1, E2 (measured relative to the ground state), of tangent fermions in the 3–4–5–0 model on an L-site 1D lattice (anti-periodic boundary conditions, bond dimension χMPS = 16384). Data points with error bars (see App. A 2) are the numerical results, the dashed line is what we would expect for a gapless system (case I in Fig. 2). A gap opening without a degenerate ground state (case III) appears in panel d) in the presence of both the 3–4–5–0 interaction (g1 = g2 = 3.5) and a sufficiently strong Hubbard interaction (K < 2/5).

FIG. 4. DMRG results for the momentum dependent occu- pation factor nα(k) of a right-moving charge (equivalently, α = 3 or 4), computed for L = 20 at three different MPS bond dimensions χMPS.
